label: early copy steps (outputs 2-3) when the current or next output is "o"
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost always at the first two copy-input steps (recall_idx 1: 70% of mass, recall_idx 2: 26%), i.e. when outputting original tokens 1-2 just after <DEL> and the echoed first token. It never fires during the original phase or on the delimiter step. Magnitude depends mostly on whether the letter o is being output now or next: out_tok = o has 17x lift and next_out = o has 12x. The top activations (~0.85-1.0 of max) are sequences beginning X o o ..., at the step right after <DEL>, with a weaker second activation (~0.4) on the following step. Without o there is a broad weak baseline (~4% of early copy steps, small activations), a bit higher for outputs k, p, m, 2, z, t, r, 3. Restricting to early copy steps captures 96% of the mass but has 11% precision. The o-conditioned predicate has 72% precision and 63% of the mass, but misses the weak non-o tail. It is mildly suppressed by digit-heavy sequences and long L (8-9).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: o, k, p, m, z, 2; least: 0, b, y, s) and the next token to output (most: o, r, 3, l, p, k; least: q, b, s, y); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, recall_idx=2, t=7.
